findings.text: Provides cached mapping service for ACPI physical ranges and publishes it through a global hook so firmware-facing code can obtain accessible views.
Exposes lookup of firmware identifier for a logical processor with range and presence checks, reporting distinct failures for out of range versus unassigned entries.
Defines general highest performance level as 196 and preferred-core highest level as 166.
Tracks preferred-core support as unknown, supported, or unsupported with a cached boost reference that becomes stable after first assessment.
Reports collaborative performance control usability from vendor and silicon generation coverage, otherwise deferring to architectural feature indication.
Fixed-hardware register access isolates a caller-defined field on a chosen processor, preserving neighboring bits on modification and always reporting availability.
Establishes frequency invariance reference from nominal capability and boost level as a midpoint between boosted and baseline throughput.
Chooses boost reference based on asymmetry presence, special silicon range, and core efficiency class, reusing cached data when uniform and querying hardware for low-power classes.
Obtains per-processor peak capability via architectural register when present, else via generic performance service, delivering a stable copy to the caller.
Determines asymmetry by sampling online processors for divergent peaks, caching the verdict and first observed peak for reuse.
Installs turbo and ceiling frequency ratios and activates capacity scaling support.
Enabling scalable frequency tracking is single-shot with diagnostic on reentry, enrolling resume support upon first success.
Resume enrollment for invariance has build-dependent presence, either registering a handler or remaining inert.
A dedicated mutex guards single publication of AMD invariance state, consulted only when required hardware capabilities exist.
Cache maintenance need and arbiter handling for deep sleep derive from online count plus vendor generation, clearing software intervention on recent designs.
Sleep hint storage is a per-processor array with one address and control pair per firmware sleep index, reached through a global per-processor anchor.
Native sleep beyond halt is denoted by register offset 2.
Acceptance of firmware sleep hints depends on processor capability, addressing, hardware substate and break support, with successful entries gaining recorded hints and vendor-specific status tuning.
Sleep and offline parking for the current processor reuse recorded hints through low-level wait primitives.
Offline parking remains in a monitored wait on a per-processor signal with cache maintenance, persisting until release or diverting to halt repetition for image replacement.
Hint storage is limited to selected vendors, created during early setup and torn down with anchor clearing on exit.
Trampoline for firmware handoff drops global translations, adopts a caller-provided identity table, then jumps to a caller-provided reset target without returning.
Wake mailbox address plus reset vector and table reference reside in post-init immutable storage with a separate active mapping pointer.
Multiprocessor stop and park paths share common offline preparation before entering the identity-mapped reset trampoline.
Confirmation of handoff to firmware allows about one second for command clearance, logging on timeout while continuing.
Early delay approximates microseconds by repeating a short port wait.
Reset readiness requires identity coverage for active ranges plus reset and trampoline pages, with multiprocessor operations and cached physical references established together.
Secondary startup requires first-use channel mapping, ordered publication of target and vector, and firmware clearance before reporting success.
After adopting firmware wakeup, further offlining is forbidden and the channel address is erased to block reuse by later images.
Wakeup descriptor handling validates presence and size, caches the channel address, and prepares reset support when versioned data allows.
